title: Semiprime algorithm proof explorer
intro: The boundary hybrid now has exact original-binary factor-byte correctness, a deterministic half-exponent checked leaf, and a closed quantitative bound for its own mixed native report. The complete primitive-machine bit-complexity theorem remains open.
target_scope: For every semiprime N from its canonical binary input, ℓ = ⌈log₂(N+1)⌉, with fixed C and d chosen before N. This is a target, not an achieved running-time theorem.
pipeline_disclaimer: This is a curated algorithm reading order, not a Lean-extracted dependency graph. Native hybrid gains and historical physical components retain their distinct cost scopes; adjacent stages do not assert complete physical caller joins.
evidence_disclaimer: Finalized means recorded historical component gates with their original scope. New native results are classified separately as mathematical proofs; compiled integration audits are separate evidence. The inventory and explorer check source/evidence hashes and do not themselves run Lean or certify whole primitive-bit running time.

glossary.meaning: A theorem identifies the specified algorithm’s output. It does not by itself establish a primitive machine’s total running time.
A fixed physical program and its stated local contract passed the recorded focused gates. Read its input boundary: a prepared operand is not automatically acquired from N.
A physical program passes actually acquired words to the next program, paying for copies, parsing, cleanup, memory and returns.
One deterministic original-input program factors every semiprime within the displayed bound, including preprocessing, recursive coefficients, storage and factor recovery.
